newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps- Gas oil slips on physical fear.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps- Gas oil slips on physical fear.

text.p: Singapore gas oil swaps shed some of its early gains late on Friday as fears of more low physical offers overcame initial optimism brought about by firm overnight crude and gas oil futures in London, traders said.
"The market is nervous as some people feel that the worst may not be over as we continue to see physical offers at low levels," one trader said.
Gas oil swaps were last quoted at $26.00/$26.10 per barrel up from Thursday's $25.85/$25.95 but about 20 cents below the morning highs, brokers said.
The market traded earlier at $26.25 and 26.10 per barrel.
February Brent crude closed up 41 cents to $23.18 per barrel on London's International Petroleum Exchange (IPE) while February gas oil was up $7.50 per tonne to $212.00 on Thursday.

Traders said the Singapore market is weighed down by surplus prompt gas oil cargoes with some sellers forced to offload on a floating price basis at about 30 cents below Singapore spot quotes, free-on-board basis.

The front month regrade or jet fuel/gas oil spread is steady at current wide levels amid strong buying interest for prompt physical jet fuel cargoes which has stretched the physical spread to a high of over $5.00 per barrel.
The February swaps regrade was last quoted notionally at $3.90/$4.30 per barrel from Thursday's $3.80/$4.00, brokers said.
On Thursday, 150,000 barrels of physical jet fuel traded at $30.75 per barrel while gas oil was offered to a low of $25.30 per barrel, both on a free-on-board (fob) Singapore basis.
Fuel oil swaps was unchanged from the morning at $100.50/$101.50 per tonne, up 50 cents from Thursday.
Naphtha rose in line with the crude hike with February quoted at $24.30/$24.60 per barrel from Thursday's $24.10/$24.30 per barrel, one broker said.
